title: Image-cokernel filtration for a finite ideal of scalars
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and let $\mathcal C$ be an abelian $A$-linear category [def-weil-linear-category]. Let $r:\iota\to A$ be a finite family, set $I=(r_i\mid i\in\iota)$, and let $m\in\mathbf N$. Suppose an object $F$ satisfies $a\operatorname{id}_F=0$ for every $a\in I^{m+1}$. Then there is a short exact sequence $0\to F_1\to F\to F_3\to0$ such that $a\operatorname{id}_{F_1}=0$ for every $a\in I^m$ and $a\operatorname{id}_{F_3}=0$ for every $a\in I$. This includes the empty family and $m=0$.

source.place: Tag 0G1T, lemma-derived-vanishing-mod-I, finite scalar-ideal filtration; explicit categorical construction is already proved in WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.DerivedCategory.TorAmplitudeResidueIdeal.

proof.text: Form the finite sum of copies of F and the morphism phi whose i-th component is r_i times the identity. Take F1=image(phi) and F3=cokernel(image.ι phi). The canonical image-cokernel sequence is short exact. If a lies in I^m, then a phi is zero, because each a r_i lies in I^(m+1); cancel the image epimorphism and monomorphism to conclude a id_F1=0. Each r_i id_F factors through image(phi), so is zero on F3 after canceling its cokernel epimorphism. Linear combinations then show that every element of I acts as zero on F3.
